considered.reasoning: Every archive signal has one identified tail and one residual tail, which is why Sharpe ratios stay near 0.2 even when alphas are large; this construction defines both tails explicitly and should improve the raw spread's risk-adjusted quality, not just its alpha. It is a genuinely different aggregation structure — a difference of two conjunctions — rather than another product of ranks.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DividendRetrenchmentByWeakEarner
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(dvc, 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(lt, at))))))
considered.hypothesis: A reduction in common dividends is an unambiguous admission of financial pressure when it comes from an already fragile firm, and such retrenchment should be followed by continued underperformance rather than a valuation rebound.
considered.reasoning: All financing legs tested so far measure capital raised or shares retired; a dividend *cut* is a distinct, discrete, and highly visible financing event that management resists until forced, so it should carry different information than issuance volume. Coverage should stay near 0.12 as in the earlier dvc-based signal, and this tests whether the fragility conditioner generalises beyond churn to payout retrenchment.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LargePayoutFromSolventEarners
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(lt, at)))))
considered.hypothesis: A credible long leg requires an affirmative action, not the absence of one: large cash distributions by firms with sustained earnings and light liabilities signal both undervaluation and genuine affordability.
considered.reasoning: Long legs built on quiescence — low issuance, contracting balance sheets, clean accruals — produced fmb t-stats up to 4.98 with zero alpha because they are spanned by CMA and RMW; a leg built on *large observed payout* is an activity measure that no FF5 factor directly represents. It also mirrors DistributionsByWeakEarners (alpha −0.015 with the weak-quality conditioner), so if the solvency-conditioned mirror delivers a comparable positive alpha, the payout-times-solvency interaction is real and two-sided.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: RankLinearizedDistressChurn
considered.expression: RANK(MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(lt, at)))))))
considered.hypothesis: The economic content is unchanged — fragile firms churning their capital structure underperform — but the score should enter a cross-sectional regression as a uniform variable rather than as a right-skewed product of ranks.
considered.reasoning: The leading signal's decile spread is strong (alpha −0.028, t −3.05) while its Fama-MacBeth slope is comparatively weak (−2.19), the classic symptom of a non-linear regressor whose slope is estimated inefficiently even when the sort is informative. A global rank is a monotone transform, so the sorted portfolios and the alpha should be essentially preserved while the fmb t-stat rises; this isolates estimation form from economics and tells us whether the family's fmb ceiling is real or mechanical.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CoverageWeightedDistressChurn
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Fragility is better measured by the ability of cash earnings to service the liability stack than by the size of the stack relative to assets; a firm with large liabilities but ample cash earnings is not fragile at all.
considered.reasoning: The liabilities-to-assets conditioner is a stock measure that mislabels asset-heavy but cash-generative firms as distressed, whereas cash earnings over total liabilities is a flow-to-stock coverage ratio that directly captures debt-service capacity. Because the quality-leg upgrade from ROA to ROA-plus-leverage produced the single largest alpha gain in the run, refining that same leg with a sharper distress concept is the highest-expected-value change available at full coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DollarEquityFlowChurn
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), SUMRANK(ABS(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), at)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(lt, at))))))
considered.hypothesis: Share-count growth measures dilution in units, not dollars; the change in book equity not explained by earnings measures the actual dollar value of equity raised or returned, and adding it should sharpen the measurement of capital-structure activity.
considered.reasoning: Share count is contaminated by splits and small option grants and misses the price at which equity was transacted, so the churn leg is currently measured with error that attenuates both statistics. The clean-surplus residual (change in common equity minus income) is dense, dollar-denominated, and captures issuance and repurchase symmetrically, making it a natural third channel alongside share-count and debt activity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AdditiveSolvencyMinusChurn
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(lt, at)))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))))
considered.hypothesis: If the return pattern is driven by two independent main effects — solvency is good, capital-structure churn is bad — then a simple additive contrast should reproduce the family's performance without any interaction term.
considered.reasoning: This is the control the archive lacks: it uses the identical two legs as the leading signals but combines them additively, so comparing it to the MIN-based two-sided spread (alpha +0.028, t +3.05) directly measures how much the conjunction contributes. A materially weaker alpha here would confirm that the interaction, not the sum of two themes, is generating the abnormal return, which is the central claim of this research direction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ChronicDilutionEventsAtFragileFirms
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_COUNT(INDICATOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 0.05), 5)), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(lt, at))))))
considered.hypothesis: Repeated recourse to the equity market — counted as the number of years in five with material dilution — identifies firms whose business model requires outside funding, and this chronic dependence is most damaging where the balance sheet is already fragile.
considered.reasoning: Summing financing magnitudes over three years destroyed the effect (t −1.60) because large one-off transactions dominate the sum, but counting discrete dilution *events* measures frequency rather than size and is robust to those outliers. This tests the chronic-dependence idea with an estimator that the earlier persistence failure did not actually rule out, using a threshold high enough (5% annual dilution) to exclude routine option grants.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitableDebtRetirement
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)), IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: Repaying more long-term debt than is issued, while sustaining solid profitability, is a voluntary transfer of risk off the balance sheet that signals confidence in future cash generation and reduces financial distress exposure.
considered.reasoning: Every long leg tried so far was either quiescence (spanned by CMA and RMW, fmb up to 4.98 with zero alpha) or payout (no information at all), leaving net debt retirement as the one affirmative, unpriced financing action untested. Debt retirement is not an FF5 factor — CMA reflects asset growth, not liability composition — so a profitable deleverager's spread has a genuine chance of surviving the five-factor adjustment.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConsolidatedChurnCoverage
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), SUMRANK(ABS(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), at)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose capital structure moves in large dollar amounts — in share count, in book equity beyond earnings, and in debt — while their cash earnings barely cover their liability stack are managing a funding problem, and their subsequent returns are poor.
considered.reasoning: Gen 5 produced two independent leg upgrades that each raised fmb from −2.19 to −2.72, one on the financing side (dollar equity flows) and one on the quality side (cash-earnings coverage of liabilities), and only the financing upgrade preserved the −0.028 alpha. Combining them is the direct consolidation test of whether the two improvements are additive in evidence, at essentially unchanged coverage near 0.13.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TwoSidedCoverageChurnSpread
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), SUMRANK(ABS(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), at)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))))))
considered.hypothesis: The investable spread runs from firms with strong debt-service coverage and a quiet capital structure to firms with weak coverage and heavy capital-structure activity, and both tails should be scored explicitly.
considered.reasoning: The additive two-sided form matched the conjunction exactly while delivering a positive Sharpe (0.117 versus −0.075 for the one-sided product), meaning it produces the same abnormal return with a better-behaved raw spread. This version upgrades both of its legs with the gen-5 winners, so it is the natural candidate for the run's final consolidated signal rather than a new mechanism.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GrossFlowsPerProfitEngine
considered.expression: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ADD(sstk, prstkc), ABS(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1))), MA(SUB(revt, cogs), 3)), 1))
considered.hypothesis: The right yardstick for financing activity is the firm's normal profit engine, not its asset base: a dollar of capital-market traffic is trivial for a firm generating large gross profits and existential for one that is not.
considered.reasoning: Scaling financing by three-year average gross profit produced the two largest fmb t-stats in the archive (−4.70, −4.52), while scaling by assets produced the alphas; this applies the profit-engine denominator to the *magnitude* concept that actually generates alpha, rather than to net issuance as before. It is deliberately parsimonious — one ratio, no rank product — so it isolates the scaler as the sole design change.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitScaledChurnAtFragileFirms
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ABS(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib)), ABS(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1))), MA(SUB(revt, cogs), 3)), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(lt, at))))))
considered.hypothesis: Capital-structure activity measured relative to the profit engine, and then conditioned on balance-sheet fragility, should carry both a sharper cross-sectional slope and the abnormal return the fragility conditioner delivers.
considered.reasoning: Signal 3 tests the profit-engine scaler alone at reduced coverage; this tests the same scaler inside the proven fragility interaction using dense balance-sheet flows, so together they separate the contribution of the denominator from the contribution of the conditioner. If both statistics improve here, the run has a signal with fmb near −3 and alpha near −0.03 at full coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConditionalSlopeNetFinancing
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(lt, at))))))
considered.hypothesis: Financing direction should matter only where the firm is fragile: raising capital is uninformative for a robust firm but is a stress signal for a weak one, so the slope on net financing should scale with fragility and vanish at strong firms.
considered.reasoning: The archive shows the current family is behaving additively, which means no genuine interaction has yet been demonstrated; centering the financing leg with IND_ZSCORE and multiplying by a non-negative fragility weight builds an explicit varying-slope interaction that is zero for robust firms by construction and cannot be replicated by any sum of main effects. This is the sharpest available test of the project's core economic claim, and its result determines whether the final signal should be interactive or additive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CoverageOnlyFragilityChurn
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Debt-service coverage alone — cash earnings relative to total liabilities — is the sufficient statistic for the fragility that makes financing activity informative, and the separate profitability channel is redundant with it.
considered.reasoning: The fragility leg has grown to two and three channels without a test of whether one suffices; dropping the ROA term while keeping coverage isolates whether the amplifier is solvency risk or simply low profitability. A comparable alpha here would justify a materially simpler final signal, and a materially weaker one would prove the two quality channels are economically distinct rather than duplicative.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SlopeOnCoverageFragility
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Net capital raising has no return implication for a firm whose cash earnings comfortably service its liabilities, and an increasingly negative implication as that coverage deteriorates; debt-service capacity is the correct measure of the fragility that activates the financing signal.
considered.reasoning: This crosses the two gen-6 leaders directly, taking the varying-slope structure that produced fmb −5.03 and Sharpe −0.506 and substituting the coverage-only fragility weight that produced the best alpha (−0.029, t −3.22). Both changes are individually validated and act on different legs, so the cross is the highest-probability route to a signal that is simultaneously strong cross-sectionally and in portfolio form.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DollarSlopeOnDualFragility
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), at), RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), IND_RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: The financing slope is best measured in dollars actually raised — share-count growth plus book equity created beyond earnings plus net debt added — and is steepest for firms that are both unprofitable and unable to cover their liabilities.
considered.reasoning: The clean-surplus equity residual improved the magnitude signal's fmb from −2.19 to −2.72 without alpha loss, and it has never been tested in signed form inside the varying-slope structure where direction, not magnitude, is what matters. Pairing it with the two-channel fragility weight gives the richest version of the mechanism, which is worth one slot even though gen 6 warns that stacking upgrades can backfire.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SlopeOnChurnMagnitude
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: If what matters is the intensity of capital-structure activity rather than its direction, then centering the *magnitude* measure and weighting it by fragility should reproduce the varying-slope gains.
considered.reasoning: Gen 6 changed two things at once — signed instead of absolute financing, and IND_ZSCORE instead of IND_RANK — so I cannot attribute the fmb jump from −2.99 to −5.03 to either. Holding the z-score weighting fixed while reverting the financing leg to magnitude cleanly separates the two effects and settles whether the final signal should be directional or intensity-based.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GatedSlopeAtUncoveredFirms
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))), INDICATOR(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3)), -0.15))
considered.hypothesis: The financing signal switches on discretely rather than gradually: only firms whose three-year cash earnings fall below roughly fifteen percent of total liabilities are constrained enough for capital raising to reveal stress.
considered.reasoning: A linear rank weight assumes the slope rises smoothly with fragility, but funding constraints are threshold phenomena, and a hard gate concentrates both extremes of the sort in genuinely constrained firms while parking unconstrained firms harmlessly at zero in the middle of a signed distribution. This is the one place where an INDICATOR does not create a degenerate tail, so it is a legitimate test of discrete versus smooth conditioning.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SlopeOnEarningsQuality
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1), dp), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Capital raising is most adverse for firms whose reported earnings are inflated by working-capital accruals, because those firms both need cash they are not generating and can sell securities into an inflated valuation.
considered.reasoning: The varying-slope structure has only ever been weighted by solvency; earnings quality is an economically distinct conditioner that was strong cross-sectionally in earlier generations (fmb up to 4.98) but never entered a slope construction. Testing whether the slope mechanism generalises beyond solvency tells us whether we have discovered a general "financing informativeness" result or a specific distress result.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DirectionPlusIntensityAtFragileFirms
considered.expression: SUMRANK(MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3)))), MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Fragile firms are penalised both for the direction of their financing (raising rather than returning capital) and for the sheer intensity of their capital-structure activity, and these are separable pieces of information about the same firms.
considered.reasoning: The two gen-6 leaders share a fragility conditioner but differ in which financing corner they identify — the slope signal shorts fragile *raisers* while the magnitude signal shorts fragile *restructurers* — so their spreads should overlap only partially and combine constructively. Averaging their ranks is the natural consolidation for a final signal, targeting the slope signal's fmb near −5 alongside the magnitude signal's alpha near −0.029.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConvexFragilityChurnSlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Financing distress is convex in coverage: the marginal harm of capital-structure activity rises sharply as cash earnings approach zero relative to liabilities, rather than increasing linearly across the whole coverage distribution.
considered.reasoning: The z-score discovery showed that preserving distributional shape in the financing leg materially improved every statistic, yet the fragility weight is still a flat uniform rank that treats the move from the 50th to 60th percentile of fragility as equal to the move from the 90th to 100th. Squaring the rank produces a convex weight that concentrates the interaction in genuinely uncovered firms while leaving the ordering monotone, which is the direct analogue of the change that worked.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DollarFlowChurnSlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), SUMRANK(ABS(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), at)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Capital-structure activity is best captured by three complementary channels — units of shares created or retired, dollars of book equity moved beyond earnings, and dollars of debt added or repaid — because each misses transactions the others catch.
considered.reasoning: The clean-surplus equity-flow channel improved fmb from −2.19 to −2.72 without alpha loss when the churn leg was rank-weighted, but it has never been tested under the z-score weighting that generated the champion. This is a single-element change to the winning expression with an independent prior of success, and it keeps coverage at 0.13.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EquityOnlyChurnSlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Discretionary equity activity — large dilution or large retirement — is the channel through which management reveals its assessment, and debt movements are largely mechanical consequences of operations.
considered.reasoning: Under rank weighting, dropping debt churn cost about a quarter of the alpha (−0.021 versus −0.028), but that test used the inferior weighting scheme and the inferior fragility measure, so the decomposition needs to be rerun on the champion's skeleton. Establishing whether a two-variable signal matches a four-variable one is essential before the final generation commits to a specification.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LossFrequencyWeightedChurn
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_COUNT(INDICATOR(ib, 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The fragility that makes financing activity informative is a history of repeated operating losses, which erodes access to capital and internal funds far more reliably than any single-year balance-sheet ratio.
considered.reasoning: Every fragility weight tested has been a contemporaneous ratio; counting loss years over five is a persistence-based, unit-free measure of chronic weakness that is robust to accounting scale and to one-off write-offs. It is the last economically distinct conditioner available, and because it is a count it produces a coarse, stable weight whose portfolio membership should turn over slowly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LiabilityScaledChurnSlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), lt)))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Debt activity should be measured as a refinancing rate against the existing liability stack rather than against total assets, because the relevant question is how much of the firm's obligations are being renegotiated.
considered.reasoning: The fragility leg is already expressed relative to liabilities, so scaling the debt channel the same way aligns numerator and conditioner and removes the distortion whereby asset-light firms register small debt deltas despite refinancing most of their debt. It is a one-line scaler change to the champion, testable at unchanged coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConjunctiveFragilityChurnSlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm is truly fragile only if it fails on both counts — poor debt-service coverage and weak profitability — and a weight built as the conjunction of the two should identify that state better than either alone or than their average.
considered.reasoning: Averaging the two quality channels via SUMRANK diluted the alpha (t −2.48 versus −3.22 for coverage alone) because a firm strong on one channel can still score high, whereas MIN requires weakness on both and has never been tried as a weight. This distinguishes "the second channel is redundant" from "the second channel was aggregated badly", which is the remaining open question about the quality leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DualScaledChurnSlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), SUMRANK(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), lt))))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Debt restructuring is economically meaningful both relative to the asset base it funds and relative to the liability stack being renegotiated, and averaging the two views measures the activity with less error than either alone.
considered.reasoning: Asset scaling delivered the best alpha (−0.032, t −4.12) and liability scaling the best slope and Sharpe (−4.94, −0.475), and the two differ only in denominator, so their average should inherit most of both rather than trade one for the other. This is the run's primary consolidation candidate, built exclusively from validated elements at unchanged 0.128 coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LiabilityScaledConjunctiveChurn
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), lt)))), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm is fragile when it fails on both coverage and profitability, and its debt activity is most informative when measured against the liabilities being refinanced.
considered.reasoning: Gen 8 produced exactly two improvements over the champion's slope and Sharpe, one on each leg, and they act on independent parts of the expression, so combining them is the natural second consolidation. Both raised fmb toward −5 with Sharpe near −0.46, so the union targets a signal that is simultaneously the strongest cross-sectionally and the best-behaved as a tradeable spread.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DebtMarketActivitySlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(dltis, dltr), lt)), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Gross traffic in the long-term debt market — issuance plus retirement measured against the existing liability stack — is the specific action that predicts poor returns at firms whose cash earnings cannot service their obligations.
considered.reasoning: The equity-only test showed the share-count channel contributes slope but no alpha, which implies the debt channel is the alpha source; this is the mirror test that isolates debt activity directly, using gross issuance and repayment flows rather than the netted balance-sheet delta. A strong alpha here would identify the mechanism precisely as debt refinancing pressure and justify the modest coverage cost of using cash-flow-statement debt items.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EquityUnitsPlusDebtMarketSlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), RATIO(ADD(dltis, dltr), lt))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Combining discretionary equity activity with gross debt-market traffic captures total capital-market dependence better than netted balance-sheet changes, which cancel an issue against a repayment made in the same year.
considered.reasoning: Netting is the one measurement flaw the champion still carries: a firm that refinances its entire debt stack registers a delta near zero. Pairing gross debt flows with the equity channel that supplies the cross-sectional slope tests whether removing the netting bias lifts both statistics, and it directly complements signal 3 by showing whether the equity channel still adds anything once debt traffic is measured properly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LeverageConjunctiveChurnSlope
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))), IND_RANK(RATIO(lt, at))))
considered.hypothesis: The binding fragility condition is a large liability stack that cash earnings cannot cover; requiring both high leverage and weak coverage identifies firms whose financing activity is compelled rather than chosen.
considered.reasoning: The conjunctive weight worked with profitability as the second channel (t −3.81, Sharpe −0.447), but profitability is largely redundant with the coverage numerator, whereas leverage intensity is redundant with nothing and was the original conditioner that first lifted alpha to −0.028 back in gen 3. Substituting leverage for ROA in the conjunction is a single-element change that tests whether the second channel should measure obligation size rather than earnings power.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: RefinancingWithoutGrowth
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(ABS(GROWTH(csho, 1)), ABS(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at)))), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3))), IND_RANK(NEG(GROWTH(at, 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Heavy capital-structure activity means opposite things depending on what it funds: paired with asset growth it is expansion, but at a shrinking, uncovered firm it is forced refinancing and the prelude to distress.
considered.reasoning: Every signal in this family treats all churn at fragile firms alike, yet the economics differ sharply between a firm raising and deploying capital and one recycling its balance sheet while the asset base contracts; requiring both weak coverage and no asset growth isolates the latter. This is the last distinct economic refinement available, and because it conditions on the absence of investment it should also reduce any residual overlap with the CMA factor, protecting the FF5 alpha.
